purpose: Define conservative Phase 5-F screening rules for high-rise humanitarian vertical evacuation candidates while preserving the boundary between official evacuation facilities and non-official emergency candidates.
lifeFirstPrinciple: During tsunami risk, life safety is the first priority. Non-official high-rises may be screened as humanitarian emergency candidates, but uncertainty and non-official status must remain visible.

layerSeparation.officialLayer: Official/designated evacuation facilities require official Chuo, Tokyo, or administrative evidence.
layerSeparation.humanitarianCandidateLayer: Humanitarian emergency candidate high-rises are non-official or unverified buildings with possible vertical evacuation potential. They are not official shelters.
layerSeparation.nonClaim: Do not label non-official candidate buildings as official evacuation shelters.
layerSeparation.officialLayerRule: candidateLayer may be official only when officialDesignationStatus is official_designated or official_designated_with_review and official source evidence is present.
layerSeparation.humanitarianLayerRule: candidateLayer must remain humanitarian_candidate for all non-official, unknown, not evaluated, conflicting, or not recommended screening records, even when physical suitability is strong.

statusTaxonomy.description: Official evidence confirms the facility/building and the building identity is sufficiently clear.
Official evidence exists, but match, source date, facility extent, or metadata ambiguity remains.
Non-official high-rise candidate with strong physical suitability evidence and manageable operational uncertainty.
Non-official candidate with promising physical signals but unresolved access, management, seismic, route, or capacity uncertainty.
Non-official candidate with limited positive evidence, weak vertical refuge margin, or substantial unresolved uncertainty.
Insufficient evidence to recommend or reject the building.
Evidence suggests the building should not be treated as a vertical evacuation candidate.

confidenceLevels.description: Official evidence or high-quality physical evidence is strong and residual uncertainty is low.
Evidence is plausible but has visible source, access, seismic, route, or management limitations.
Evidence is weak, incomplete, conflicting, or relies mainly on inferred candidate suitability.

signals.exampleRule: Height at least 30 meters or floorsAboveGround at least 10 supports strong high-rise candidacy.
Height at least 15 meters or floorsAboveGround at least 5 may support weak or review-level candidacy.
Confirmed or estimated seismic evidence improves physical suitability but does not certify safety.
Larger floor area or estimated capacity proxy improves screening priority when source uncertainty is visible.
Location in tsunami risk context can increase humanitarian relevance, not official status.
Route distance/time that is not obviously impossible can support candidate screening.

signals: management agreement unknown or not found
source date or source authority missing

conservativeScoringPolicy.missingCriticalEvidenceRule: Missing height, floor, capacity, route, seismic, public access, or management evidence must reduce confidence, increase operationalUncertaintyScore, and may downgrade status from strong to review, weak, unknown, or not_recommended.
conservativeScoringPolicy.officialSeparationRule: High physical suitability, low route distance, or high capacity can never upgrade candidateLayer to official without official designation evidence.

classificationGuidance.notes: Must remain non-official unless official evidence is later added.
Use when physical evidence is promising but access, seismic, route, or agreement uncertainty is unresolved.
Use when there is some vertical refuge signal but not enough for a strong candidate.
Use when evidence is too incomplete for candidate or rejection.
Use for low-rise, unsafe, underground-only, practically inaccessible, or conflicting evidence cases.

publicAccessPolicy.rule: Unknown public access must not automatically exclude a building in the humanitarian emergency scenario, but it must trigger manualReviewNeeded, reviewRisks, reviewTriggers, and warnings.

downgradeOrNotRecommendedSignals: height below 12 meters and floorsAboveGround below 4
known seismic concern without mitigating evidence
underground-only or no usable upper-floor refuge
known demolition, closure, or building condition issue
route access practically impossible in the modeled context
conflicting evidence that would make candidate labeling misleading
requiredWarningRules: Every non-official humanitarian candidate must warn that it is not an official shelter.
Unknown public access must be preserved as uncertainty.
Unknown management agreement status must be preserved as uncertainty.
Unknown seismic evidence must be preserved as uncertainty.
Life-first emergency access is a scenario assumption, not a legal or official access guarantee.
Prototype route estimates must not be called official evacuation routes.
